feed.title: The 3 Best 6G Stocks to Buy in August 2024
feed.summary: This article identifies InterDigital (IDCC), SK Telecom (SKM), and Apple (AAPL) as the top three 6G stocks to consider buying in August 2024. It highlights 6G technology's potential for ultra-high speeds and near-instantaneous response times, projecting significant market growth. The piece details each company's relevance to 6G development and their strong financial performance, making them attractive investments in the burgeoning 6G market.

feed.title: Intel Corporation (New Mexico)
feed.summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce has awarded Intel up to $7.865 billion in direct funding through the CHIPS and Science Act to expand its capacity and capabilities across four U.S. states. This funding supports Intel's plan to invest nearly $90 billion to create a robust domestic semiconductor ecosystem, anticipating 10,000 manufacturing and 20,000 construction jobs. Specifically, the Rio Rancho, New Mexico facility will receive $500 million to modernize two fabs into the largest advanced packaging facility in the U.S., creating 1,800 manufacturing jobs and 2,500 construction jobs.

feed.title: Intel shares slump 26% as turnaround struggle deepens
feed.summary: Intel's shares dropped 26% in their worst day since 1974 after the company suspended its dividend and announced a 15% workforce reduction to fund a costly turnaround strategy. The move, aimed at catching up with competitors like TSMC, resulted in a market value loss of over $30 billion. The disappointing forecast and job cuts have deepened investor concerns about Intel's ability to regain its once-dominant position in the chip manufacturing industry.

feed.title: Intel has worst day on Wall Street in 50 years, falls to lowest price in over a decade
feed.summary: Intel's shares experienced their largest drop since 1974, plummeting 26% to their lowest price since 2013, after the chipmaker reported a significant earnings miss and announced a restructuring that includes laying off over 15% of its workforce. This downturn dragged down other global chip stocks like TSMC and Samsung, and contributed to a 2.4% drop in the Nasdaq. The company also reported a net loss of $1.61 billion, missed revenue expectations, and suspended its dividend, implementing a $10 billion cost-reduction plan.

feed.title: Intel Shares Fall by Most Since at Least 1982 on Grim Forecast
feed.summary: Intel Corp. (INTC) shares experienced their largest decline in over 40 years, falling 26%, after providing a grim growth forecast and announcing plans to cut 15,000 jobs. This move signals the chipmaker's struggles to compete in the artificial intelligence era and resulted in a $32 billion loss in market value. The company also confirmed its revenue would fall short of expectations.

feed.title: Earnings call: Aptiv reports record Q2 earnings and new $5 billion repurchase
feed.summary: Aptiv (NYSE: APTV) announced record Q2 2024 earnings and a new $5 billion share repurchase authorization, including a $3 billion accelerated share repurchase program. Despite a 2% dip in revenue to $5.1 billion, the company achieved record EPS growth of 26% and significant operating margin expansion due to strong execution and reduced supply chain costs. Aptiv revised its full-year revenue outlook downward, anticipating a 3% decrease in global vehicle production, but remains confident in its long-term growth prospects and ability to navigate market challenges.

feed.title: Intel to cut 15% jobs, suspend dividend in turnaround push; shares plummet
feed.summary: Intel announced on Thursday that it will cut over 15% of its workforce, approximately 17,500 employees, and suspend its dividend starting in the fourth quarter as part of a turnaround strategy. The chipmaker aims to focus on its manufacturing business and reduce costs while battling increased competition in the AI chip market. This news caused Intel's shares to plummet by 20% in extended trading, reflecting investor concerns about its financial outlook and its struggle to compete with rivals like Nvidia and AMD in the AI sector.

feed.title: Actions to Accelerate our Progress
feed.summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger announced significant cost-cutting measures, including a reduction of 15,000 roles (15% of its workforce) and $10 billion in cost savings by 2025. These actions are necessary to align the company's cost structure with its new operating model, address lower-than-expected revenue growth and margins, and prioritize investments in its IDM2.0 strategy by suspending the stock dividend. The plan aims to make Intel a leaner, simpler, and more agile company despite the difficult decisions involved.

feed.title: Intel Corp., major Arizona employer, to cut 15% of its workforce
feed.summary: Intel Corp. announced plans to cut 15% of its global workforce, amounting to about 1,800 positions in Arizona, as part of a restructuring to save $10 billion due to weak financial results and high costs. Despite significant investments in Arizona, including $20 billion for new fabs in Chandler and substantial CHIPS Act funding, the company is facing economic headwinds. CEO Pat Gelsinger noted slower-than-expected revenue growth and the need for "bolder actions" to address financial challenges, including offering enhanced retirement and voluntary departure programs.
